method: Downloaded arXiv v1 PDFs from arxiv.org and checked version metadata; checked Bhowmik-Grimmelt metadata at Springer. Source files retained outside the repository in /tmp/stage69_sources.

sources.title: Fourth moments of prime exponential sums and exceptional sets for sums and differences of primes
sources.hypothesis: Q_Theta: every nontrivial zero of every primitive Dirichlet L-function, including zeta, has real part <= one fixed Theta; Theorem 1 requires Theta < 11/12.
sources.result: For specified smooth Gevrey w in C_c^infty((0,1)), 0<=w<=1, w=1 on [1/8,7/8], P=X^kappa with fixed kappa(Theta) in (4/9,9/20), minor fourth moment is O_{w,Theta}(X^(5/2)(log X)^100). Theorem 2 gives square-root-log exceptional-set bounds; Proposition 4.1 gives major-arc asymptotic under fixed Q_Theta, Theta<1 and kappa<9/20.
sources.pointwise_target_consequence: No signed pointwise minor coefficient bound; exceptional-set results permit isolated exceptions.

sources.title: The Goldbach exceptional set: an exponent 7/12 and conditional refinement
sources.status: preprint; v1 checked; authors state proof not Lean verified
sources.hypothesis: H_theta0: every zero of every primitive Dirichlet L-function, including zeta, lies in Re(s)<=theta0; fixed parameter.
sources.result: Theorem 1 exceptional set O_{theta0,epsilon}(X^(7/12+epsilon)) for theta0<1. Theorem 3 under fixed theta<=2/3 gives exponent g(theta)+epsilon, g(theta)=theta(5-4theta)/(2(2-theta)); at theta=5/8 this is 25/44+epsilon.
sources.external_dependency: Cites an OpenAI/Lean 7/8 zero-boundary result; exact source build not independently identified or compiled in this audit.
sources.pointwise_target_consequence: Positive-power exceptional set does not eliminate a designated target.

sources.authors: I. Althöfer, D. Chen, A. Perelli and J. Pintz
sources.title: The exceptional set of Goldbach numbers among polynomial values
sources.hypothesis: Fixed integer polynomial with positive leading coefficient and degree k>=2; theorem constants may depend on polynomial and epsilon.
sources.result: Polynomial-indexed exceptional count O_{phi,epsilon}(N^(alpha_k+epsilon)); alpha_2=1/2, alpha_3=5/8, alpha_4=3/4, alpha_k=1-1/(k+1) for k>4.
sources.external_dependency: Uses Li-Liu and cited external zero-free input as stated in the paper.
sources.pointwise_target_consequence: Degree one is excluded; a positive-power exceptional count along a polynomial sequence does not rule out a selected residual target.

sources.title: The exceptional set of the Goldbach problem
sources.hypothesis: Theorem 3.1 assumes every zero of every Dirichlet L-function has Re(rho)<= one fixed Theta<3/4.
sources.result: Theorem 6.3 gives an explicit formula for the major-arc error E_M(N), for even N in [X/2,X] under 0<epsilon<vartheta<4/9-epsilon and R=X^vartheta, with a sum over pairs of exceptional zeros and characters plus O(X exp(-cH)+X/T+X^(1-epsilon)); it is not shown uniformly small for every target. Theorem 3.1 gives the conditional exceptional-set bound |E(X)| <<_epsilon X^(2Theta-1/2+epsilon) under the fixed all-Dirichlet-L-function zero hypothesis Theta<3/4. Neither statement is a full pointwise Goldbach asymptotic.
sources.pointwise_target_consequence: The conditional exceptional-set bound can still contain a specified isolated target.

external_openai_lean_zero_free_source.reason: Downstream citations did not provide a directly identified retrievable source file plus compiled project/build proving the precise theorem and scope; a commit identifier alone was insufficient.
external_openai_lean_zero_free_source.policy: Retain as an explicit external dependency wherever downstream papers use it; do not claim independent formal verification.

limitations: The source audit checks statements, notation, hypotheses, version metadata and scope; it is not a reproof of the analytic papers.
None of the audited sources yields unconditional signed pointwise positivity for every N in H.
The preprint source files are not checked into the repository; hashes identify the retrieved copies outside the repository.
